questions.title: Which city will be the site of Typhoon Dolphin's first landfall in mainland China in August 2026?
questions.background: Dolphin developed into a typhoon over the Pacific in late July 2026.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Landfall information issued by China's meteorological authorities, either directly or through contemporaneous reliable news coverage. Resolution Condition : Resolve to the city identified as the location of Dolphin's first mainland China landfall during August 2026. Offshore island landfalls do not count. Accepted Answer Format : Provide the city name, rather than its province or a broader geographical region.
questions.current_reasoning: Key 2026-07-29 southward shift in ensemble track guidance for Super Typhoon Dolphin (now Cat 3 at 950 hPa / 43 m/s east of Guam, forecast to reach Cat 5 / 150 kt / 915 hPa by July 31). Dr. Ryan Maue (July 29) reports both fresh 06z Google DeepMind ensembles and the dominant cluster of 00z full-physics ECMWF EPS track south of Japan along roughly 30°N latitude, while KMA/Asia Business Daily (July 29) notes ECMWF/Windy shows the North Pacific High blocking Dolphin toward waters near Okinawa (~26.2°N) and onto mainland China around August 7 (and Vietnam NCHMF confirms it will not enter the South China Sea, ruling out Guangdong). A 28°N-31.5°N corridor directly targets mainland Zhejiang and Shanghai (with offshore Zhoushan islands excluded by criteria, putting mainland Ningbo at 29.9°N right at the center of the 30°N axis, flanked by Taizhou, Shanghai, and Wenzhou), while Nation Thailand's Chawalit projection flags Jiangsu north of Shanghai (Nantong). Tightening 9-day Gaussian spread toward Ningbo (0.10 -> 0.16), Taizhou (0.09 -> 0.14), Shanghai (0.10 -> 0.12), Wenzhou (0.07 -> 0.11), and Nantong (replacing Yancheng at 0.08), leaving 39% across Ningde, Fuzhou, Yancheng, Jiaxing, and Shandong/Fujian coastal cities.

local_articles.title: 13-metre waves, 268kmph winds: Super typhoon Dolphin barrels towards East Asia
local_articles.snippet: Several East Asian countries and territories are preparing for the onslaught of yet another strong weather system that has developed into a super typhoon in the central Pacific Ocean. Super Typhoon Dolphin has become an extremely violent system near Wake Island and is barrelling towards southern Japan, northern Taiwan and mainland China as it moves westward. It currently generates extremely rough seas and high swells that are expected to impact marine areas and island regions. ST Dolphin is whipping up 13-meter waves with sustained winds of 268 kilometres per hour and gusts of up to 324 kmph as of Thursday, according to the US’ Joint Typhoon Warning Center (JTWC). The said parameters are forecast to grow even stronger in the next 48 hours, it said. Stay up to date with the latest news. Follow KT on WhatsApp Channels. It is expected to directly impact East Asian countries early next week.

questions.title: Which country's mainland coastline will be confirmed contaminated by the Caroline Bezengi oil spill by August 13, 2026?
questions.background: The Caroline Bezengi has been leaking crude oil since running aground in June 2026.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Public statements by government environmental authorities, or reliable news reports directly citing those statements. Resolution Condition : Resolve to the country whose mainland coastline is confirmed to have been contaminated by oil from the Caroline Bezengi by August 13, 2026. Offshore pollution, contamination confined to islands, and predictions of future landfall do not qualify. Accepted Answer Format : The country's name.
questions.current_reasoning: July 2 Khaleej Times reporting notes Oman's Environment Authority announced a vessel ran aground near an island in the Al Hallaniyat Islands marine reserve off Oman's Dhofar Governorate, with technical teams inspecting it July 1, sampling coastal waters around Al Hallaniyah Island, coordinating with Oman's National Committee for Emergency Management, and stating there is 'no evidence of any oil pollution so far' while urging the public to avoid 'fake news.' Because the Caroline Bezengi was already reported leaking crude oil since running aground before June 24 and Khaleej Times does not name the vessel, this Al Hallaniyat grounding is more likely a separate Khareef-monsoon incident (~85%), though there is a non-trivial ~14% chance it is the unnamed shadow-fleet Caroline Bezengi (or that Oman is reassuring residents about inhabited Al Hallaniyah Island specifically), in which case Oman's mainland Dhofar coast sits ~40 km directly downwind/downcurrent. Combined with peak July Southwest Monsoon winds/East Arabian currents pushing any Socotra/Gulf-of-Aden slick northeastward toward Oman's Dhofar/Al Wusta coast and Oman's much stronger environmental authority reporting infrastructure (critical under the Source of Truth clause), we shift Oman up from 0.35 to 0.42 and trim Yemen from 0.46 to 0.40 (Somalia 0.09, India 0.04, Djibouti 0.02; 3% tail).

questions.title: Which country will agree to a joint project with Iran to clear sea mines from the Strait of Hormuz by August 26, 2026?
questions.background: Sea mines have been reported near the Strait of Hormuz, a major route for international oil and gas shipments.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Resolve to the country that agrees with Iran to a joint mine-clearance project in the Strait of Hormuz, as announced in a statement from the two governments by August 26, 2026. Resolution Date : 2026-08-26 Accepted Answer Format : Answer with the country's common English name.
questions.current_reasoning: Important July 28 diplomatic updates (Reuters/Straits Times, Al Jazeera, Khaleej Times, Irish Times): amid a third straight night of halted US-Iran airstrikes, Iran and Oman formally exchanged written proposals on reopening and managing the Strait of Hormuz — Oman proposed a Malacca-style joint regional mechanism with voluntary fees, while Iran's Deputy FM Kazem Gharibabadi counter-proposed a temporary Iran-Oman transit arrangement. Crucially, Gharibabadi explicitly warned that Tehran 'would not allow any third country, even if invited by Oman, to de-mine the Strait of Hormuz' (as the US and UK discuss a Western demining coalition in London), while Al Jazeera reports Tehran is privately showing 'some flexibility' in step-by-step bilateral talks with Muscat even though mine-clearance responsibility remains a point of contention. Because Oman is the sole co-littoral state negotiating directly with Tehran and Iran just publicly ruled out third-country demining participation, Oman strengthens meaningfully (0.37 -> 0.44, still moderated below 0.50 since no joint mine-clearance pact is signed and Tehran currently prefers unilateral clearance). Third-country alternatives trim modestly: China (0.25 -> 0.22), Pakistan (0.16 -> 0.14), and Russia (0.09 -> 0.08), with Japan held at 0.02 and 10% residual for UAE, Turkey, India, Qatar, or others.

local_articles.title: Can China Restrain Iran? Gulf States Test Beijing's Influence
local_articles.snippet: Riyadh: As the Iran war escalates again, Gulf Arab states are looking to China - not Washington - to use its economic leverage over Iran to open up the Strait of Hormuz and Red Sea, testing how far Beijing is able and willing to pressurise Tehran. The Gulf push for a bigger Chinese role is driven by growing frustration, Gulf sources say. The war launched with US-Israeli attacks on Iran on February 28 has hurt their regional foe but also restricted their vital energy exports and, to varying degrees, put them in the firing line. With Iran and its allies threatening the Bab el-Mandeb waterway in the Red Sea as well as Hormuz, Gulf states have sought Beijing's help, conscious that the war has exposed the limits of American power, three regional sources say. local_articles.title: Omani, Nepali climbers dead after avalanche strikes Pakistan's Broad Peak; 8 missing
local_articles.snippet: Omani climber Nadhira Al Harthy and Pur Bahadur Gurung “Yukta” of Nepal died after an avalanche struck Pakistan's Broad Peak (8,047m) in the Karakoram mountain range, when the two were on a climbing expedition with eight others, the Alpine Club of Pakistan confirmed. The UAE hiking and mountaineering community mourned Al Harthy "whose passion, courage, and achievements inspired climbers across Oman and the Arab world", in an Instagram post by Arabian FiTrekkers. The identities of the remaining climbers will be confirmed and shared as soon as official information becomes available, the club added. The expedition comprised eight other people — including five more Nepalese, a Pakistani, an American, a climber from China, and one other foreigner. Stay up to date with the latest news. questions.title: Which DRC province will WHO identify as experiencing a surge in weekly Ebola cases in mid-September 2026?
questions.background: The Democratic Republic of Congo declared an Ebola outbreak in May 2026.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : WHO public statements about the DRC Ebola outbreak, including statements quoted in contemporaneous reputable news reporting. Resolution Window : Resolve to the province explicitly identified by WHO as experiencing surging weekly Ebola cases in its outbreak assessment publicly reported between September 10 and September 16, 2026. Accepted Answer Format : The name of the province.
questions.current_reasoning: Hard provincial data from DRC INSP SitRep 073 (published July 27, data to July 26: 3,262 cases, 1,437 deaths) alongside July 30 Al Jazeera/AP updates (3,442 confirmed cases, 1,521 deaths—a 50% one-week death spike with 50 deaths in 24 hours; Uganda declared Ebola-free July 28): (1) North Kivu overtakes Ituri for #1 (0.29 -> 0.35) after reaching 314 confirmed cases and 204 deaths, with Ebola treatment center bed occupancy jumping from 120% (July 21) to 136.2% (192 patients for 141 beds) plus 11 infected health workers—signaling an accelerating secondary wave in Katwa/Butembo/M23-affected corridors well positioned for a mid-September WHO weekly surge call. (2) Ituri remains strong at #2 (0.32 -> 0.31) with 2,901 cases (88.9% of total) and 1,207 deaths amid July 28 Bunia health worker strikes, the Nyakunde facility attack, and 60.9% community deaths. (3) Haut-Uele rises to #3 (0.13 -> 0.15) with 38 confirmed cases and formal inclusion in the expanded four-province UN Ebola response appeal. (4) Tshopo drops sharply to #4 (0.19 -> 0.12) after holding flat at 5 confirmed cases with zero new cases from July 21 to July 26, confirming containment of Kisangani's imported cluster so far while retaining river-corridor re-introduction risk. (5) South Kivu stays at 0.02 (3 cumulative cases, 61 consecutive days with zero new cases; 5% residual for Bas-Uele/Maniema/Kinshasa).

questions.title: Which European country will announce a complete drought-related shutdown of its nuclear power generation between August 1 and August 13, 2026?
questions.background: Nuclear reactors require reliable cooling-water supplies. Low river levels can force reactors to shut down, potentially disrupting national electricity supplies.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Official announcements by national nuclear operators or governments, corroborated by reliable news reporting. Resolution Conditions : Identify the European country that announces, between August 1 and August 13, 2026, a shutdown covering its entire operating nuclear fleet because drought has left insufficient river water for cooling. An announcement initiating the shutdown of the last operating reactor qualifies; a partial shutdown alone does not. Accepted Answer Format : The country's common English name.
questions.current_reasoning: Major 2026-07-30 Danube nuclear reversal reshapes the Aug 1-13 complete-fleet shutdown race (BBC, DW, Reuters/Straits Times, BTA July 30): (1) Hungary surges to #1 (0.23 -> 0.41): Paks halved Unit 2 output Thursday morning (after shutting Unit 3 Wednesday and cutting Unit 1 Monday), PM Peter Magyar warned Hungary's only nuclear plant will be forced to shut down entirely because suction nozzles cannot reach the record-low Danube, and Paks' operator stated a complete shutdown is unavoidable within 24 to 72 hours (July 31-Aug 2); capped at 0.41 solely because of the ~45-50% timing risk that the announcement initiating shutdown of the final operating reactor happens on July 31 (before Aug 1). (2) Romania rebounds sharply to #2 (0.08 -> 0.29): despite Nuclearelectrica's July 29 warning, Unit 2 remained connected to the grid on July 30 as conditions allowed overnight operation, leaving Romania with only 1 operating unit while Danube inflow is forecast to drop further from 1,600 m3/s to 1,500 m3/s by Aug 4—putting an Aug 1-4 final-reactor shutdown squarely back in play (discounted modestly for July 31 timing and July 29 pre-announcement criteria friction). (3) Bulgaria drops sharply to #3 (0.50 -> 0.23): Kozloduy NPP stated July 30 afternoon (BTA) that both Units 5 and 6 are operating normally on schedule, citing its deep-bay shoreline pumping station and upstream Iron Gate (Djerdap) dam water-level coordination with Serbia; retains solid Aug 4-13 weight if Hungary and Romania complete shutdown announcements before Aug 1. Slovenia (0.11 -> 0.04) and Switzerland (0.05 -> 0.01) fall with zero late-July warnings (sum 0.98).
